ShortDescription.Value: UK-style junction rules for drivers and yellow box junctions they actually obey.

Publish.LongDescription:
Junction Rules makes traffic behave more like real (UK-style) traffic at junctions, crossings and building driveways, and adds painted **yellow box junctions** that drivers actually obey.
## Getting started
Open **Options → Junction Rules** and set **Car driving** to **Junction Rules** (it starts on the game's own driving, so nothing changes until you switch). For the whole-junction gap rule below, also set **Junction gap rule** to **Whole junction**. Every rule can be switched on or off on its own, and **Car driving: Game's own** brings back stock behaviour at any time, also in a running city.
## How it works
The game's car-driving system is switched off and replaced by a Burst-compiled copy of it with Junction Rules' changes inside. The copy is checked against the game's own code at load: if the game updates and the code no longer matches, the mod falls back to the game's driving and the **Status** line in Options says why.
## Junction rules
- **Whole-junction gap.** A car that has to give way stops at one spot, just before the first place its path crosses another lane, and decides once for the whole junction: it goes only when every conflict on its path is clear for the time it needs to get through. It never creeps into a junction and stops halfway across another lane. Vehicles stopped at a red light don't count as approaching. - **Turning across oncoming traffic gives way.** Straight-ahead traffic has priority over vehicles turning across it (right turns in left-hand traffic, left turns in right-hand traffic). - **Zebras.** People on a zebra have priority: cars never push through them, and cars don't stop on a zebra unless there's room past it for the whole vehicle. If a car does end up blocking a crossing, people walk past it after a short wait (2 s by default), so nobody is trapped. - **Unmarked crossings.** People give way to cars instead of cars giving way to people. Cars only wait for people actually crossing, not for someone standing at the kerb. - **Leaving and entering buildings.** A vehicle leaving any building treats the pavement like a zebra and pulls out only when people, the lanes it crosses and the lane it joins are all clear, with room for its whole length. A vehicle turning into a building across oncoming traffic gives way to that traffic.
## Yellow boxes
- Open the tool with **Ctrl+Y** or the toolbar button. Hover a junction or a building: a white outline means click to add a box, orange means click to remove it. Boxes are saved with your city. - Each real car access of a building (exit, entrance or two-way) is boxed on its own. - Boxes have straight sides, kerb to kerb, and never cover zebras, stop or give-way lines or medians. Boxes closer than a car length merge into one. No parking inside a box. Road markings under a box can optionally be hidden. - A vehicle enters a box only if there is room past it for its whole length (trailers included): free right now, or, with the setting Look past the car in front at a box (on by default), free by the time it gets there, with every vehicle ahead expected to keep going and to stop only behind a queue or vehicle it can see standing (crawling slower than about 18 km/h counts as standing), or at a red light (within its 100 m line of sight; nothing slow in sight means it goes). The vehicles ahead are packed nose to tail, never in another yellow box, on a zebra or in another junction. Otherwise it stops with its front bumper at the line. - UK exception (optional): a vehicle turning across oncoming traffic may wait inside a junction box when its exit is clear and only oncoming traffic stops it. - The mod never adds a starvation timeout: a vehicle that can't go legally waits. - Some spots can't take a box (elevated or tunnel roads, highways, roundabouts and so on); the tool says why.
## Compatibility
- Built for game version 1.6.4. After a game update the mod falls back to the game's own driving until it is updated. - Saves stay loadable without the mod: boxes are stored as small components the game skips when the mod is missing. - Works alongside Traffic (lane connections, priorities) and Road Builder roads. - Not compatible with other mods that replace the game's car driving system.
## Source and issues
Source code, issue tracker and design notes: https://github.com/durianpeople/cs2-junction-rules (MIT licence for Junction Rules' own code; the copied game code remains the property of Colossal Order / Paradox Interactive).

ChangeLog.Value: Since 1.0.0: - Yellow boxes: cars look past the car in front, up to 100 m. They enter when nothing within sight is stopped or slow, or when the queue they can see would still leave room for them past the exit (counted without standing in another box, on a zebra, in another junction or on a level crossing). Trucks, buses and buildings block the view. Turn "Look past the car in front at a box" off for the old rule. - Yellow boxes: a car may enter and wait for people walking across the exit zebra when there is room beyond. - Signalised junctions: a zebra whose pedestrians have red no longer holds cars back; they may wait on it, but never while the exit is blocked. - Building entrances: each access is boxed on its own (boxing one no longer boxes another), and the Ctrl+Y hover target covers the road and the strip to the access. - Select a car and each change in why it slows is written to Logs/JunctionRules.Mod.log.
